batch_strategy: Condition-response series with targeted failure repair. The batch emphasizes amount and loading-solvent-volume contrasts where recent labels showed endpoint-specific or nonlinear effects, then adds sulfur, carbonyl, nitrile and high-retention graph segments to repair structural extrapolation and endpoint-slope errors.

choices.reason: m72 at 2/1, 50-ul PE loading starts a fixed-medium amount series. It tests whether the strong amount dependence seen at 10/1 DCM between 7383949c431e18f39597 and a2f83665cfe821271b30 persists at a different solvent ratio.

m72 at 2/1 and 100 ul PE supplies the middle amount point between the selected 50-ul and 150-ul rows. A smooth or nonmonotonic endpoint response will constrain how amount and eluent strength interact.

m72 at 2/1 and 150 ul PE completes the amount series. It is useful because the current predictions are nearly amount-invariant while the measured m72 responses at other ratios are strongly condition-dependent.

m92 at 2/1, 50-ul EA loading begins a matched three-amount segment. The 20/1 EA series 66da447ca0fe7160cc1c, 8b58e9d7a710f55e49d3 and e9dc948c0e68a88eb621 showed an unusual amount pattern that should be tested at a stronger eluent.

m92 at 2/1 and 100 ul EA provides the interior amount point for the stronger-eluent series, separating a genuine amount response from the previously observed 20/1 trough and its nonmonotonic midpoint.
m92 at 2/1 and 150 ul EA completes the matched amount series. Jointly with the two lower amounts, it can teach whether V1 and V2 share the same loading dependence.

m125 at 1/1, 50 ul sample and 500-ul DCM loading volume is one half of an exact loading-solvent-volume comparison with 00043aebb2540e369a7b. The measured 5/1 pair 74cf50c6ec476a394b01 and c4b5a5499258f39b7ac1 showed a large onset shift with nearly unchanged completion.

m125 at 1/1 with 300-ul DCM loading volume provides the matched reference for f4fb5c03b8e8996e75f6. Repeating the volume contrast at another ratio tests whether the observed onset sensitivity generalizes beyond the prior 5/1 pair.

m125 at 5/1, 150 ul sample and 500-ul DCM loading volume extends the volume-controlled series beyond the measured 100-ul rows. It tests whether completion remains stable while onset changes with loading context.

m125 at 5/1, 50 ul sample and 500-ul DCM loading volume supplies the low-amount point paired with 06ebbf6e52fa3ea6aef3. Together with the measured 100-ul volume contrast, this separates amount and loading-volume effects.
m127 at 5/1 and 50 ul PE loading tests a missing ratio segment against the strong onset-by-amount behavior measured at 20/1 by 8143c4fff6f999b7ad0e and ebdeaba52880c7eade16.

m127 at 5/1 and 100 ul PE is the midpoint of the new amount contrast. The measured 50/1 midpoint a3ae677aae8a8faf5786 was a large onset outlier, so this label tests whether the nonlinearity is ratio-specific.

m127 at 10/1 and 100 ul PE compares a third ratio at the same nominal amount. It discriminates a common loading shift from the ratio-specific onset curves seen in 15d6bc57a87392fbeb98 and a3ae677aae8a8faf5786.
m128 at 2/1 and 50 ul DCM loading tests amount dependence beside the measured 2/1, 100-ul result 21e09d52eac22fe25e15 and the measured 5/1 response 892c3900698d3de38b1c.
m128 at 5/1 and 150 ul DCM extends its sulfur-containing ketone curve to a higher amount. It tests whether the measured 5/1 onset and completion remain transferable across loading amount.

m129 at 0/1 supplies a strong-eluent anchor for the aldehyde analogue. The measured m129 responses at 5/1, cf8ab33c25ad391a584c, and 20/1, f4331eb64b6774466836, already suggest a nontrivial local curve.
m129 at 1/1 fills the adjacent sulfur-aldehyde segment and tests whether its endpoint response changes smoothly from the proposed 0/1 point toward the measured weaker-eluent labels.

m199 at 1/1 and 50 ul DCM adds a low-amount interior to the diphenyl-sulfoxide curve. The measured 0/1 anchor b2bf97a1dcb9d6609f7d and the 5/1 amount pair f82cfd3b57735b0ead3c and 6bd128bde2e137ea54f3 show that sulfur oxidation state needs its own response surface.
m199 at 2/1 and 100 ul DCM tests an interior ratio and amount after the large 10/1 failure aa83ae83c0fa0cc37777. It can distinguish a steep ratio transition from a broad amount effect.

m159 at 10/1 has a broad predicted endpoint range and a distant condition context. It targets high-retention extrapolation in a nitrile-containing diaryl ketone environment, where ordinary carbonyl transfer may fail.

m191 at 5/1 and low amount probes a sparse dialdehyde curve with wide predicted completion variation. It complements the high-retention measured m191 result bae9d67e095423d8edd2 and tests whether both endpoints acquire the same weak-eluent slope.

m114 at 50/1 targets a missing weak-eluent segment with a large predicted completion range. It extends the measured multifunctional-carbonyl behavior represented by b8268449dc991ce92f3d and tests graph-specific tail growth.

m11 at 50/1 and 150 ul is a high-tail amount contrast against measured m11 at 50/1 and 100 ul, 9ffee2813aef5c26f96f. The label can teach whether the model underrepresents late completion in this polar oxime-like graph.
m78 at 50/1 and 150 ul extends the measured 50/1, 100-ul point 61771d230b285babe4b6. It supplies a controlled high-retention amount response for a multifunctional ester graph.

m172 at 0/1 adds a strong-eluent anchor to the measured 2/1, 20/1 and 50/1 curve points 9e46469e7c9719ba3611, fd11ee7c408d95a1a8e6 and 419f6eb4080dcb9d293b. It tests whether onset and completion slopes differ locally.

m103 at 0/1 completes the stronger-eluent side of a sparse ester curve. The measured 10/1, 20/1 and 50/1 labels 76d382617e5051b76435, c98657e16e93ef4ede6b and fc911fe23a3e1e8e87d2 provide slope references without assuming a common ester response.

m162 at 1/1 fills the strong-to-intermediate nitrile segment between measured 5/1, 10/1, 20/1 and 50/1 labels 862163fa99660a023b6f, c82c1933ed710ffb4981, ed3a90d38ff02a38deba and 7b8eaa0c9205349f60b1.

m167 at 2/1 samples a missing substituted-diketone segment with a narrow point prediction but high condition distance. Its label can test whether the locally smooth carbonyl transfer assumed by the model is valid at this ratio.

m31 at 2/1 and 150 ul extends a cyanoacetophenone curve into a missing ratio and amount context. Existing m31 observations such as 5ae1e9580200827a709d and b3d9bb5afa82b99f2a11 show that related carbonyl graphs can have very different tails.

m3 at 0/1 tests a remaining strong-eluent endpoint case after m71 measured ordered endpoints even where its 0/1 prediction had V2 below V1. Measured m3 points c59ffcab9329339d3e91 and 8ba04fd976f536e8340b anchor its nearby curve.

m39 at 20/1 and 100 ul fills the amount midpoint around the measured 20/1, 50-ul point 5524670e4337370c2ef6. Its large predicted tail makes it useful for learning amount-dependent completion in a diaryl carbonyl graph.

m40 at 2/1 and 50 ul adds a strong-eluent anchor to the measured m40 curve at 10/1, 20/1 and 50/1, including 594f52943fa688878ad4, b645df00945e594953a6 and 4e93e36ab850bab3d594. This tests whether the model can transfer the graph-specific onset slope.

hypotheses.content: Endpoint-order and endpoint-shape failures are local graph-condition problems. The m71 0/1 prediction violated endpoint ordering even though its measured endpoints were ordered, while the exceptionally early m23 onset and extremely narrow m18 interval were also not realized; a blanket neat-EA boundary explanation is therefore inadequate.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Labels from other early-eluting graphs can teach endpoint coordination and ordering without forcing a global boundary correction that would damage ordinary rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do other strong-eluent graph contexts show ordered endpoints with a coordinated response, or do they produce distinct local endpoint defects?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount affects V1 and V2 conditionally on solvent ratio, loading medium and molecular graph. m72 showed a large 10/1 DCM amount contrast while its 5/1 DCM contrast was modest; m92 showed a nonmonotonic 20/1 amount response, so a universal monotonic loading law is unsupported.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched amount series can teach separate endpoint responses and ratio-by-loading interactions that are reusable across many catalog rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m72 2/1 PE and m92 2/1 EA amount series remain smooth, or do they reveal additional ratio-specific reversals?

hypotheses.content: m127 has strong, endpoint-specific and ratio-dependent loading behavior. The 20/1 amount series interpolated toward earlier onset at higher amount while completion stayed similar, whereas the 50/1 100-ul midpoint was an extreme onset outlier.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A ratio-specific onset response can improve interpolation for substituted acetophenones and prevent the model from pooling incompatible loading effects.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the 5/1 and 10/1 PE amount points retain the 20/1 onset trend, or do they reproduce the anomalous 50/1 behavior?

hypotheses.content: The recorded loading-solvent volume can affect retention beyond sample amount. For m125 at 5/1, changing DCM volume from 300 to 500 ul shifted onset substantially while completion remained close, although the feature is confounded with loading procedure in many catalog rows.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched volume contrasts can teach whether this recorded feature deserves a transferable correction or should be downweighted as noise.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m125 loading-volume effect persist at 1/1 and at different sample amounts?

hypotheses.content: Sulfur-containing graphs require oxidation-state and local functional-context responses beyond coarse polarity descriptors. m128 and m129 have different measured curves, while diphenyl sulfoxide shows a very different late-elution response and limited amount dependence at 5/1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local sulfur curves can prevent the model from transferring carbonyl or acceptor-count corrections across thioether, aldehyde and sulfoxide environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the missing strong-eluent and amount points produce smooth sulfur-specific curves, or do oxidation state and graph identity create separate regimes?

hypotheses.content: Endpoint slopes are graph-specific and often differ between V1 and V2. Measured carbonyl, ester and nitrile examples include flat weak-eluent onset, steep onset, unusual completion growth and large high-retention errors, so related functional groups should not share one generic solvent-response curve.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Filling missing graph-condition segments and high-retention regions can improve transfer across the Row-distribution while repairing endpoint-specific extrapolation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected high-distance graph segments follow their neighboring curves, or do they expose additional structural contexts requiring separate response terms?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes support selective condition-response repair. m71 endpoints were ordered despite a predicted V2<V1, while m23 and m18 did not realize their exceptional onset or narrow-interval predictions, weakening a blanket boundary campaign. m72 showed a large amount contrast at 10/1 DCM but little contrast at 5/1 DCM, and PE loading produced much later elution. m92 20/1 labels remained nonmonotonic across amount. m127's 20/1 midpoint interpolated its onset trend, whereas the 50/1 midpoint was an extreme outlier, strengthening ratio-specific modeling. The m125 300-versus-500-ul DCM comparison shifted onset more than completion, supporting a second volume-controlled test. Sulfur outcomes confirmed distinct m128, m129 and m199 behavior, and the m103, m33, m162, m163 and m189 labels strengthened the case for graph-specific endpoint slopes. The new batch therefore spends labels on matched curves and missing segments rather than repeating a general neat-EA boundary search.
batch_rationale: The batch has four coordinated local experiments: m72 and m92 amount series at new ratios, m127 ratio-specific amount points, and m125 loading-volume and amount contrasts. These labels directly supervise interactions that recent measurements showed to be nonlinear and endpoint-specific. Sulfur rows m128, m129 and m199 extend local oxidation-state and graph-context curves. The remaining choices target sparse or high-distance graph-condition regions, including m159, m191, m114, m11, m78, m39, m103, m162, m167 and m31, where neighboring measured rows show different onset and completion slopes or large historical misses. A single m3 boundary point checks endpoint behavior in another early-eluting graph. The batch is intentionally redundant where the rows form interpretable response curves and diverse where the model needs structural transfer; the resulting labels can improve condition handling, tail calibration and V1/V2 coordination across the Row-distribution after retraining.
